name: Ocean Blue
lede: Ocean Blue is a strong, greenish blue standardized in Germany's RAL system as RAL 5020, though the screen swatch shown here follows the brighter, more saturated value the crowd-labeled xkcd survey gave the same name.

sections.title: Two swatches, one name
sections.body:
RAL fixes its own Ocean Blue, RAL 5020, at a darker, more muted teal, hex #0B4151 [1]. The 2010 xkcd color survey uses the identical name for a brighter, more saturated blue, #03719C, and that is the value this swatch shows, so treat this page as the crowd value, not the RAL standard [1]. The ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 place the RAL region in block 174, the same broad block that also holds [[night-blue]], and attach a long run of other names to it, among them Mallard, Napoli and Teal Duck [1].

Its nearest distinct named neighbor by hue is [[peacock-blue]], 3.3 units off and "almost the same," with [[cerulean]] close by [3]. No book held in color-kb discusses "Ocean Blue" by this exact name [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Ocean Blue is rare in our archive: 19 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.08 percent, as photographed [2]. Austrian works carry it at over 10 times the archive's overall rate, the highest lift of any country we track for this color, and its earliest dated appearance is a 1482 Florentine double portrait, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
